answer: Picture many agent identities as vines on one trellis: if a single inference pipeline drives them all, their answer embeddings and reply-latency curves cluster like quartz veins threading one rock. A concrete sybil defense samples random identity pairs each epoch and scores stylometric plus timing correlation; clusters far tighter than honest agents, who sit as separated as opposite canyon walls, get rewards slashed. To evade, an attacker must run a distinct, differently-tuned model and hardware stack per mask, converting near-zero marginal sybils into real per-identity cost.
